instructions.name: start_level
docs: `boost` pays $CRUMB for a longer round; see BOOST_EXTRA_SECONDS.

errors.name: SubmittedTooSoon
errors.msg: Play a little longer before submitting a score

errors.name: ScoreImplausible
errors.msg: That score isn't plausible for how long the session ran

errors.name: BoostAccountsMissing
errors.msg: Paying for a longer round needs your Cookie Jar and its $CRUMB accounts

fields.name: crumb_balance
docs: Legacy balance from before $CRUMB became a real SPL token. Only ever
written to pre-migration; frozen (and zeroed once spent) afterward.
Cannot be removed or reordered -- every already-minted jar on-chain
has this exact byte layout baked in, and Borsh deserializes
positionally, so doing either would corrupt every existing account.

fields.name: migrated
docs: Appended field, not inserted -- new fields must only ever go at the
end for the same reason `crumb_balance` can't move. False on every
jar that existed before this field did (realloc zero-initializes new
space), true immediately for jars minted after, since they start
with nothing to migrate.

types.name: LevelScore
docs: A player's running record for one level. Persists across attempts.

types.name: Session
docs: An in-progress level attempt. Created by start_level, closed by
submit_score, so a player can only have one open attempt per level.

fields.name: boosted
docs: Whether the player paid $CRUMB for a longer round. Recorded so the
purchase is visible on chain, not because the clock is enforced here.

constants.name: BOOST_COST_CRUMBS
docs: What a longer round costs in $CRUMB. Roughly twelve seconds of a jar's
accrual, so it's a real decision without being out of reach.

constants.name: BOOST_EXTRA_SECONDS
docs: How much longer a boosted round runs, on top of the base 60. The clock
itself is client-side like the rest of the board, so this is the agreed
number both sides work from, not something the chain enforces. The
*payment* is enforced; the extra time is as trusted as the score is.

constants.name: MAX_SCORE_PER_SECOND
docs: Loose plausibility ceiling, not real anti-cheat: gameplay lives entirely in
the browser, so nothing here can prove a submitted score came from actual
play. This only rejects a score no session of that length could reach.

constants.name: MIN_ELAPSED_SECONDS
docs: A session must run at least this long before its score can be submitted,
so a session can't be opened and closed in the same instant.

constants.name: SCORE_BURST_ALLOWANCE
docs: Flat allowance on top of the per-second ceiling, so a strong opening
cascade in the first second or two isn't rejected as "too fast."
